english.title: Ship's master with HM / foreign state commission fail to account for goods loaded outside UK
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the person in command of a ship, namely **(..SPECIFY THE SHIP..), which had a commission from

(A)_[His Majesty]_
(B)_[a Foreign State, namely **(..SPECIFY THE STATE..),]_

and which had on board goods loaded in a place outside the United Kingdom and the Isle of Man, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PLACE..), failed,

(C)_[before the goods were unloaded,]_
(D)_[when called upon to do so by the proper officer,]_

to deliver to the proper officer an account of the goods in accordance with section 36(2) of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979
english.legislation: Contrary to section 36(1) of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979.

english.notes: Section 10 of the Interpretation Act 1978 states that any reference to the Sovereign reigning at the time of the passing of the Act is to be construed, unless the contrary intention appears, as a reference to the Sovereign for the time being. As such, references to ‘Her Majesty’ and ‘the Queen’ have been replaced in the wording of the offences to state ‘His Majesty’ or ‘the King’, although this may not be the strict wording of the legislation.
